title: 12 Animal Myths That Could Actually Get You Hurt (TRUE or FALSE?)
blurb:
TRUE or FALSE? Pee on a jellyfish sting, play dead for every bear, suck out snake venom... some "survival tips" everyone knows are wrong, and one could save you. Guess before the 3-second timer, keep score, and drop your score out of 12 in the comments 👇

Fun general info only: always follow local wildlife and medical guidance.
next: Subscribe for Part 5: animal facts that sound fake but are totally real.
pinned:
📝 SCORE CHECK: how many did you get out of 12? 👇

Answer key: TRUE = make yourself big for a mountain lion. Everything else was FALSE.

Which one would have gotten YOU hurt? Comment it.

beats.say: Pee on a jellyfish sting. Play dead for a bear. Suck the venom out of a snake bite. Everybody knows these. Plot twist. Some of them could actually get you hurt.
beats.text:
MYTHS THAT COULD
GET YOU HURT

beats.say: You get three seconds to guess true or false. Keep score. Only ONE of these is true, so trust nobody. Not even me. Okay, trust me a little. Quick note, this is fun general info, so always follow local wildlife and medical advice.
beats.text:
ONLY ONE
IS TRUE

beats.say: True or false? If a jellyfish stings you, you should pee on it.
beats.bonus: The pee myth got famous from a nineteen ninety seven episode of Friends.
beats.short_title: Should You Pee on a Jellyfish Sting? 🪼

beats.say: False. Please don't. It doesn't help, it can make it worse, and now the whole beach is staring at you.
A sting leaves behind tiny stinging cells. Fresh water, and yes, pee, can trigger the ones that haven't fired yet, so you get stung even more.
Let's be crystal clear. Pee is not medicine. Pee is a bathroom thing. Leave it in the bathroom.
beats.text:
PEE IS NOT
FIRST AID.

beats.say: What helps depends on the jellyfish, but common advice is to get out of the water, rinse with sea water or vinegar, and carefully lift off any tentacles without touching them with bare hands. Hot water can help with the pain.
The myth got huge thanks to a nineteen ninety seven episode of Friends. Great sitcom. Terrible first aid.
beats.text:
GREAT SITCOM.
TERRIBLE
FIRST AID.

beats.say: True or false? If any bear attacks you, you should play dead.
beats.quiz:
IF A BEAR
ATTACKS,
PLAY DEAD
beats.bonus: Black bears aren't always black. They can be brown, cinnamon, or even almost white.
beats.short_title: Should You Play Dead if a Bear Attacks? 🐻

beats.say: False. It depends on the bear, and on why it's attacking.
If a grizzly or brown bear attacks because it's surprised or protecting cubs, wildlife officials say play dead. Lie on your stomach, hands behind your neck, and stay still.
This is the one time playing dead is the plan. So commit to the role. Stay still. No peeking.
But if a black bear attacks you, don't play dead. Fight back hard, and aim for the face and nose.
And with any bear that stalks you, or tries to get into your tent, fight back. That bear isn't scared. It's interested. Bear spray, carried where you can grab it fast, is your best friend out there.
Easy way to remember it. If it's brown, lie down. If it's black, fight back. Just know a black bear can be brown, so learn the shapes, not just the colors.
beats.text:
BROWN? LIE DOWN.
BLACK? FIGHT BACK.

beats.say: Yes, nature put a trick question inside the trick question. Thanks, nature.
beats.text:
A TRICK QUESTION
INSIDE A TRICK
QUESTION

beats.say: True or false? You should suck the venom out of a snake bite.
beats.bonus: Copperheads bite a lot of people in the US, but deaths from their bites are extremely rare.
beats.short_title: Should You Suck the Venom Out of a Snake Bite? 🐍

beats.say: False. Every cowboy movie lied to you. Every single one.
Sucking a bite pulls out almost no venom, and it puts mouth germs right into a fresh wound. Cutting the bite open or tying a tight tourniquet can make things worse too.
The real plan is boring but it works. Move away from the snake, stay as calm and still as you can, take off rings or tight stuff near the bite because it can swell, and get to a hospital fast.
So no sucking, no cutting, no cowboy stuff. Just calm, and a hospital.
beats.text:
NO COWBOY
STUFF.

beats.say: Hospitals have antivenom. Your mouth does not.
beats.text:
HOSPITALS HAVE
ANTIVENOM.
YOUR MOUTH
DOES NOT.

beats.say: True or false? If a crocodile chases you, run in a zigzag.
beats.quiz:
RUN IN A
ZIGZAG FROM
A CROCODILE
beats.bonus: When resting, crocodiles can stay underwater for more than an hour.
beats.short_title: Should You Run Zigzag From a Crocodile? 🐊

beats.say: False. Zigzagging just makes your escape longer. You are not dodging lasers.
Crocodiles are lightning fast at the water's edge, but on land they tire quickly and rarely chase far. So the best move is to run straight away from the water, as fast as you can.

The real danger zone is the edge of rivers and lakes. Most crocodile attacks happen at the water, when someone is drinking, washing, fishing, or swimming. Stay well back from the bank in croc country.
In croc country, the riverbank is the crocodile's front porch. Do not hang out on its porch.
beats.text:
DON'T SIT ON
THE CROC'S
PORCH.

beats.say: So no fancy moves. Straight line. Away from the water. Go.
beats.text:
STRAIGHT LINE.
AWAY FROM
THE WATER.

beats.say: True or false? Moose are gentle giants that won't hurt you.
beats.bonus: Moose can run around thirty five miles an hour, and they are excellent swimmers.

beats.say: False. Moose look like a horse that was drawn from memory. But they are seriously dangerous.
Alaska wildlife officials say moose injure more people there each year than bears do. A moose can weigh more than a thousand pounds and kicks with its front hooves.
Warning signs are ears laid back, the hair on its back standing up, and lip licking. If you see that, back away. If it charges, run and get behind something big like a tree or a car.
Ears back, hair up, lip licking. That's not a moose saying hello. That's a moose counting down.
The good news is a moose usually won't chase you far. It just wants you gone. Honestly, same.
beats.text:
IT JUST WANTS
YOU GONE.

beats.say: True or false? Jumping into water is a good way to escape angry bees.
beats.quiz:
JUMP IN WATER
TO ESCAPE
ANGRY BEES
beats.bonus: Stinging bees release an alarm smell that can remind people of bananas, and it tells other bees where to attack.
beats.short_title: Can You Escape Bees by Jumping in Water? 🐝

beats.say: False. The bees just wait for you to come up for air.
Angry bees can hover over the water and keep stinging the moment you surface. That's a much worse situation than before.
Instead, run away in a straight line, cover your face, and get inside a building or a car as fast as you can. Don't swat, because that just makes them angrier.
I know. Every part of you wants to swat. Don't swat. Just go.
beats.text:
DON'T SWAT.
JUST GO.

beats.say: Cartoons taught us water is a force field. It's actually a waiting room.
beats.text:
WATER ISN'T A
FORCE FIELD.
IT'S A WAITING
ROOM.

beats.say: True or false? Hippos are slow, lazy animals that won't chase you.
beats.quiz:
HIPPOS ARE
TOO SLOW TO
CATCH YOU
beats.bonus: Hippos can't really swim. They walk and bounce along the bottom of rivers.
beats.short_title: How Fast Can a Hippo Run? 🦛

beats.say: False. Don't let the chunky look fool you. Hippos are one of the most dangerous large animals in Africa.
They can run around nineteen miles an hour on land in short bursts. That's faster than most people can sprint.
So if your plan was to outrun a hippo, get a new plan. Preferably one that starts far, far away.
They are extremely territorial, especially in the water, and a hippo can flip a boat that gets too close. They look like they are napping. They are not napping. They are watching.
So that big yawn you see in photos? That's not a yawn. That's a warning.
beats.text:
NOT A YAWN.
A WARNING.

beats.say: True or false? A rattlesnake always rattles before it bites.
beats.bonus: A rattlesnake adds a new rattle segment every time it sheds, so counting them doesn't tell you its age.
beats.short_title: Do Rattlesnakes Always Rattle Before Biting? 🐍

beats.say: False. Lots of rattlesnakes stay totally silent.
A rattlesnake's first plan is to hide. Its camouflage is amazing, so it often just freezes and hopes you walk past. If you step close before it notices, there might be no warning at all.
So in snake country, watch where you put your hands and feet, step on top of logs instead of over them, and stay on the trail.
Basically, in snake country your feet need a supervisor. That supervisor is your eyes.
beats.text:
YOUR FEET NEED
A SUPERVISOR.

beats.say: The rattle is a courtesy, not a promise.
beats.text:
THE RATTLE IS A
COURTESY, NOT
A PROMISE.

beats.say: True or false? If you meet a mountain lion, make yourself look as big as you can.
beats.quiz:
MOUNTAIN LION?
MAKE YOURSELF
LOOK BIG
beats.bonus: Mountain lions can't roar. They purr, hiss, and make chirps that sound a lot like birds.
beats.short_title: What Do You Do if You Meet a Mountain Lion? 🐆

beats.say: True! Finally! This one is real advice.
Stand tall, raise your arms, open your jacket, and speak in a loud, firm voice. You want to look like something that isn't worth the trouble.
And whatever you do, don't run. Running can trigger the cat's chase instinct. Face it, back away slowly, and pick up small kids so they don't run either. If it attacks, fight back.
So the recipe is big, loud, and backing away slowly. This is not a race you want to enter.
beats.text:
DON'T RUN.
BE BIG.
BE LOUD.

beats.say: So basically, become the biggest, loudest, most annoying thing on that trail. For once, it's a good strategy.
beats.text:
BE THE BIGGEST,
LOUDEST THING
ON THE TRAIL

beats.say: True or false? Ticks jump on you, or drop on you from trees.
beats.quiz:
TICKS JUMP OR
DROP FROM
TREES
beats.bonus: Ticks wave their front legs to grab passers-by, which scientists call questing.
beats.short_title: Do Ticks Jump or Fall From Trees? 🕷️

beats.say: False. Ticks can't jump or fly, and they don't dive out of trees. No ninja ticks.
They wait on tips of grass and low plants with their front legs stretched out, which is called questing. When you brush past, they grab on, then crawl upward.
So ticks aren't acrobats. They're hitchhikers. Tiny hitchhikers holding out their legs instead of their thumbs.
beats.text:
TICKS DON'T
JUMP. THEY
HITCHHIKE.

beats.say: That's why they turn up on your head even though they started near your ankles. After a hike, check behind your knees, your armpits, your waist, and along your hairline.
If you find one attached, grab it close to the skin with fine tweezers and pull straight out, slow and steady. No matches, no nail polish.
beats.text:
TWEEZERS.
SLOW AND STEADY.
NO MATCHES.

beats.say: True or false? Opossums usually carry rabies.
beats.bonus: Opossums have fifty teeth, more than any other land mammal in North America.

beats.say: False. Rabies is actually rare in opossums.
Scientists think one reason might be their fairly low body temperature, which may make it harder for the virus to take hold.
And that scary hissing face with all the teeth? Mostly a bluff. When it's really scared, an opossum may play dead, drool, and give off a stinky smell. And it can't control it. It just happens.
Imagine your whole defense plan is drool and a bad smell. Bold strategy, little buddy.
So the possum is not a rabies monster. It's a nervous little guy who faints for a living. Still, never handle wild animals.
beats.text:
NOT A MONSTER.
IT FAINTS FOR
A LIVING.

beats.say: True or false? That fluffy caterpillar is safe to pet.
beats.quiz:
THIS FLUFFY
CATERPILLAR IS
SAFE TO PET
beats.bonus: The puss caterpillar grows up into a fluffy moth called the southern flannel moth.
beats.short_title: Is It Safe to Touch a Fuzzy Caterpillar? 🐛

beats.say: False. This is the puss caterpillar, and it's one of the most venomous caterpillars in the US.
Under all that soft-looking fur are hidden venomous spines. Touch it, and people describe the pain as intense, burning, and spreading, sometimes for hours.
It lives on trees and shrubs in the southern United States, and it often turns up on fences, walls, and playgrounds. Kids want to pet it, which is exactly the problem.
Fluffy does not mean friendly. Look with your eyes, not your fingers.
beats.text:
FLUFFY DOES NOT
MEAN FRIENDLY.

beats.say: Rule of thumb. If a caterpillar looks like a tiny toupee, do not touch the toupee.
beats.text:
DO NOT TOUCH
THE TOUPEE.

beats.say: Scores! The only true one was making yourself big for a mountain lion. Everything else was false. Yes, all of it. Drop your score out of twelve in the comments, and tell me which one surprised you most.
beats.text:
COMMENT YOUR
SCORE /12
